To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the main sources for information about complementary and alternatives medicine (CAM) are general practice and community pharmacy and that physicians are concerned about adverse effect while pharmacists are more concerned about interactions.
questions about CAM are mainly patient-specific, come from general practice and community pharmacy, and are mainly about herbs, vitamins and mineral products, interactions, and adverse effects.

questions about complementary and alternative medicines (CAM) to the Regional Medicine Information and Pharmacovigelance Centres in Norways (RELIS) were mainly concerned about interactions (33%), adverse effects (16%) and documentation (38%).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the provision of clinically relevant information to health care professionals about CAM.
the information needs of health care professionals about CAM and not the information needs of CAM users.
the provision of information about CAM to health care professionals in a real-life setting.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the provision of information about CAM to health care professionals in Norway is insufficient.
the information about CAM in RELIS is insufficient.
RELIS is a valuable source of information to health care professionals about CAM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the questions about CAM to our information service are mainly about documentation and interactions, and that the lack of information to answer the questions is not significantly different between general and patient-specific questions.
we are not yet prepared to provide the necessary information about CAM to our health care professionals, and that we need more research in order to be able to do that.
we have a lot of work to do.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the need to provide clinically relevant information about CAM is present and the need to improve the provision of information about CAM to health care professionals should be addressed.
more information about CAM is needed to provide answers to health care professionals in their daily practice.
the information needs of health care professionals about CAM are diverse and that the provision of clinically relevant information is not well described.
